Class DockElement

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<DockElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.DockElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class DockElement extends StyledElement<DockElement>
A 5-region dock layout element that arranges children into top, bottom, left, right, and center regions — the most common TUI application structure (header + sidebar + content + footer).

Extends StyledElement directly (not ContainerElement) because it has 5 named regions, not a positional children list.

All layout properties can be set via CSS or programmatically. Programmatic values override CSS values when both are set.

Supported CSS properties:

  • dock-top-height — height constraint for the top region
  • dock-bottom-height — height constraint for the bottom region
  • dock-left-width — width constraint for the left region
  • dock-right-width — width constraint for the right region
  • margin — margin around the dock layout
  • background — background color fill

Example usage: 

dock()
    .top(text("Header").bold())
    .bottom(text("Footer").dim())
    .left(text("Sidebar"))
    .center(text("Main Content"))
    .topHeight(Constraint.length(3))
    .leftWidth(Constraint.length(20))

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size
